step1_analysis.description: A stacked RF front-end consisting of a common-source LNA with a cascode device, driving a current-commutating quadrature mixer. The RF signal is amplified and converted to current, which is then split into I and Q branches by common-gate transistors and mixed with LO signals to produce downconverted IF outputs.

paper_reference.title: A 2-GHz CMOS Image-Reject Receiver With LMS Calibration

power_consumption.description: Total DC power consumed by the LNA and mixer stack.

sky130_expected.calculation: Id ~ 54uA based on W/L=5/0.5 and Vov=0.2V. Power = 1.8V * 54uA = 97uW. With larger bias, up to 1mW.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The provided W/L ratios are small (5um/0.5um), leading to very low current compared to the full receiver in the paper.

conversion_gain.description: Voltage conversion gain from RF input to IF output.

sky130_expected.calculation: gm1 = 0.54mS. Rload = 10k. Gain = (2/pi) * gm1 * Rload = 3.4 V/V = 10.6 dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Depends heavily on the chosen load resistors, which are added in the testbench since they are not in the netlist.

lna_gain.description: Voltage gain at the LNA output node (N4).

sky130_expected.reasoning: The LNA output is a current-mode interface to the mixer, so voltage gain at this intermediate node is near unity.

noise_figure.description: Noise figure of the receiver front-end.

sky130_expected.calculation: Standard LNA NF is 2-3 dB, mixer adds 2-3 dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Expected to be slightly higher than the paper due to the small W/L and low bias current in this specific netlist.
The paper's 17 dBm is very high, likely achieved with specific linearization techniques or higher bias currents not present in this bare netlist.

operating_frequency.description: The RF frequency the circuit is designed to receive.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure DC power, LNA voltage gain, and RF-to-IF conversion gain.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Testbench for LNA and Quadrature Mixer
.param W_xm3=5u L_xm3=0.5u
.param W_xm8=5u L_xm8=0.5u
.param W_xm2=5u L_xm2=0.5u
.param W_xm4=5u L_xm4=0.5u
.param W_xm6=5u L_xm6=0.5u
.param W_xm1=5u L_xm1=0.5u
.param W_xm7=5u L_xm7=0.5u
.param W_xm5=5u L_xm5=0.5u

.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

* DUT
XM3 N9 N0 N3 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm3} w={W_xm3}
XM8 N1 LO_Q N6 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm8} w={W_xm8}
XM2 N4 VB2 N11 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm2} w={W_xm2}
XM4 N7 LO_I N9 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm4} w={W_xm4}
XM6 N6 N0 N3 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm6} w={W_xm6}
XM1 N11 VIN N5 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm1} w={W_xm1}
XM7 N10 LO_Q_BAR N6 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm7} w={W_xm7}
XM5 N2 LO_I_BAR N9 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm5} w={W_xm5}

* Connections
V_N4_N3 N4 N3 0
V_N5 N5 0 0
V_N0 N0 VB1 0

* Power Supply
VVDD VDD 0 1.8

* Biases
VVB1 VB1 0 1.1
VVB2 VB2 0 0.8
VVIN_DC VIN_DC 0 0.6

* RF Input (2.4 GHz, 10mV peak, AC=1 for AC analysis)
VRF VIN VIN_DC dc 0 ac 1 sin(0 10m 2.4G 0 0)

* LO Signals (2.21 GHz, 400mV peak, 1.4V DC)
VLO_I LO_I 0 dc 1.4 sin(1.4 0.4 2.21G 0 0 0)
VLO_I_BAR LO_I_BAR 0 dc 1.4 sin(1.4 0.4 2.21G 0 0 180)
VLO_Q LO_Q 0 dc 1.4 sin(1.4 0.4 2.21G 0 0 90)
VLO_Q_BAR LO_Q_BAR 0 dc 1.4 sin(1.4 0.4 2.21G 0 0 270)

* Loads
R1 N7 VDD 10k
R2 N2 VDD 10k
R3 N1 VDD 10k
R4 N10 VDD 10k

.control
  * 1. DC Power
  op
  let power_w = -i(VVDD) * 1.8
  print power_w

  * 2. AC Analysis for LNA Gain
  ac dec 10 1G 10G
  let lna_gain = vdb(N4)
  meas ac lna_gain_24g find lna_gain at=2.4G
  
  * 3. Transient Analysis for Conversion Gain
  tran 5p 50n
  let v_if_i = v(N7) - v(N2)
  meas tran if_max max v_if_i from=30n to=50n
  meas tran if_min min v_if_i from=30n to=50n
  let if_pp = if_max - if_min
  let rf_pp = 0.02
  let conv_gain = if_pp / rf_pp
  let conv_gain_db = 20 * log10(conv_gain)
  print conv_gain_db
  
  quit
.endc
